name: Puragi
confidence_why: The only description that marks Puragi stress, de Vries's 2004 survey wordlist in the Inanwatan grammar, places it on different syllables from word to word and states no rule, and Voorhoeve's 1975 checklist wordlists explicitly leave stress unmarked, so no source determines the system.
catalog_citation: de Vries, Lourens. 2004. A short grammar of Inanwatan, an endangered language of the Bird's Head of Papua, Indonesia. Pacific Linguistics 560. Canberra: ANU. Appendix 3 'Survey data of the languages of the Inanwatan district', sec. 2 'Puragi', pp. 137-142.
catalog_locator: Appendix 3, sec. 2.1 'phone inventory' and 2.2 'Word list (Puragi dialect)', pp. 137-140 (lines 6455-6700 of sealang)

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: The deciding quotation is verbatim in the PL-560 text we hold at the stated appendix/pages. The classification 'undetermined' rests on the best (indeed only) stress-bearing description of Puragi: de Vries's 2004 survey appendix, which marks stress on a 209-item list but states no rule, and the marked stresses visibly vary in position (initial, second, third, fourth syllable), consistent with the record's the primary-stress rule. Glottolog lists zero grammars/sketches/phonologies for Puragi (Glottolog's most extensive description = this wordlist); the other held survey (Berry & Berry 1987) and the newly downloaded Voorhoeve 1975 ('Stress and pitch are not indicated') are silent.
